correctness.rationale: The minimax proof is valid. Removing the support and at most two neighbors for each prescribed positive leaves a bipartite graph; its larger side plus the positives yields the stated ceiling lower bound. The upper-bound trace is built recursively by excluding the first vertex if it is in the support, allowing at most one selection in the first two positions if both are outside the support, or prescribing the second vertex positive and excluding its two neighbors; the short bases and the ceiling update check out. All-positive forces independence and size at most k. Capacity at least k for every trace is sufficient by trimming outside its positive vertices. Spacing compression gives the binomial counts. For d≥1, 3d≤n+1, and every maximal independent set dominates the path and hence has at least ceil(n/3) vertices. For an independent check of shellability without relying on the unavailable Björner–Wachs copy: in any path forest with all maximal independent sets of size at least d, choose the neighbor v of a leaf u when there is an edge. In the deletion of v every maximal independent set contains the now isolated u and is maximal in the original, so has size at least d. In the deletion of the closed neighborhood of v a maximal independent set has size at least d−1, by adjoining v to make a maximal set of the original. These two smaller forests give the deletion and link of the rank-d truncation at v, of ranks d and d−1, with no common facet. Induction gives pure vertex decomposability, starting at rank zero and at edgeless graphs (ordinary simplex skeletons, with the same deletion/link induction). Pure shellability gives the wedge, whose multiplicity is (−1)^(d−1) times reduced Euler characteristic as stated. For d=0 the complex consists of the empty face and no sphere-wedge conclusion is needed. Neither recorded field homology nor finite trace checks establish all-parameter topology.

evidence: For a path with a support of s independent positions, use the s+1 segments between consecutive padded boundaries/support vertices. With prescribed bits a,b on a segment of length L, the prior mismatch bit δ is L−(a xor b) modulo 2. Its lower bound of δ zero-zero edges is attained by the prior alternating-segment construction with δ inserted edges. Interior segments have L≥2, so with endpoints 11 the remaining even length is at least 2, as required to visit a zero. If the number of changing edges is 0 or 1, the endpoints are not both 1; the constant zero segment or one change with zeros inserted realizes the bound. This also handles a segment of length 1 at a padded endpoint.

Consequently the exact maximal trace extension has size (n+1−sum δ)/2. The prior §6 says the mismatch vectors range over the binary vectors of total parity n+1; their largest weight is s+1 or s according to parity. Substitution gives precisely ceil((n−s)/2) as the worst extension. All-positive and trimming give the criterion as in the frozen proof. For n=2k−1, outside the earlier cycle parameter range, there is just the unique alternating size-k path set, so only the empty support is shattered; n≤2 is direct.

From the criterion the face count is the ordinary path-independence count up to rank d. The purity inequality is an immediate domination bound, and the topology and alternating rank then follow from standard pure shellability and Euler characteristic.
